Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.45% today to $457.22, continuing a decline that's picked up pace over the last week—down nearly $21 from its peak on October 16th. The timing is notable: the stock turned downward just as oil prices spiked sharply on geopolitical tensions. While high crude prices typically benefit refiners, the market appears concerned that the spike is driven by Middle East conflict risk rather than stable demand. At the same time, U.S. refinery utilization sits at a healthy 93.4%, so the pullback isn't about weak operations or low margins.

The broader issue may be uncertainty itself. Oil prices have swung dramatically on Iran-related headlines—Brent jumped above $116 as tensions escalated—but those same geopolitical shocks tend to create volatility in refined product demand and can sometimes point to economic slowdown ahead. Refinery stocks can struggle in that environment even when crude prices are high, because investors worry the spike won't stick around long enough to drive profitable sales.
